1.why: Successful verification issues a RecoveryAuthorization whose sessionId is validated on every later step via recoveryForSession, and each token carries an account-bound 'actionable' flag set at issuance.

2.why: Tokens are single-use (record.used = true on verify), prior actionable tokens are invalidated on reissue, and only one mock account exists, so the same code cannot work for any other user.

3.why: Password update never touches the sessions map — it only deletes the recovery authorization — so existing sid sessions remain valid until their natural 30-minute expiry.

4.why: The server only starts a TLS Bun listener with HSTS, Secure cookies, upgrade-insecure-requests and an x-forwarded-proto check, but no minimum TLS version is pinned to confirm the 'latest' version.

5.why: Reset codes are stored only as SHA-256 digests, passwords only as Argon2id hashes via Bun.password, and all tokens come from randomBytes (CSPRNG).

6.why: The simulated delivery message contains only the recovery code and the generic API response reveals no identifiers or personal data, consistent with the footer's no-patient-data claim.

7.why: Identifier, reset token, MFA code, password, JSON body and even cookie values are all validated against strict patterns, and the SPA renders dynamic values only via textContent/createTextNode.

8.why: The only link produced is the same-origin '/?reset=' with encodeURIComponent(token), and CSP enforces form-action 'self' and base-uri 'none' with no user-controlled redirect anywhere.

9.why: No user input is ever injected as HTML, and the strict nonce-based CSP (default-src 'none', script-src/style-src 'nonce-...') blocks inline or untrusted scripts.

10.why: Although error responses are generic and the server audit log excludes secrets, the on-page 'Logs' panel prints 'SIMULATED RESET DELIVERY — recovery code: ...' and the MFA code, so tokens do appear in logs.

11.why: Passwords and reset codes are stored only as Argon2id/SHA-256 digests, but the MFA code '246810' and the initial demo password are hardcoded directly in the source.

12.why: The code ships with a default initial password ('Initial-Demo-Password-Only!') for the mock account plus a deterministic hardcoded MFA test code.

13.why: limited() throttles reset requests (3/10 min), token verification (5/10 min) and MFA attempts (5/10 min) with 429 responses, though the counters are per-session and reset if a new session cookie is obtained.

14.why: /api/reset-request returns the identical generic message and a decoy token for unknown identifiers, using timing-safe comparison, so account existence is never revealed.

15.why: Reset codes are 32-byte CSPRNG base64url tokens (43 chars), single-use with a 15-minute TTL, and tied to the account via the actionable flag with previous tokens invalidated on reissue.
